A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 51-page versions of the same work. The main text, Tables 1–12, Figures 1–8, and Appendices A–D are readable and directly comparable.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training and evaluation, perplexity-bound comparisons, and spelling-correction experiments in Section 4 and Appendix B.6.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix B.6, including language-model evaluations and spelling-correction accuracies.

M1.justification: CEDD/CEDD* objectives, ratio reconstruction and rescaling, roulette diffusion, and the time-evolving extension are unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the architecture and sampling procedures also match.

E1.justification: Both retain OpenWebText training and evaluation on LAMBADA, WikiText2, WikiText103, PTB, and 1BW. Spelling correction still uses War and Peace for training and Crime and Punishment and Pride and Prejudice for testing.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding tables: SEDD/SEDDs, CEDDT, GPT-2, D3PM, PLAID, and discrete flow matching. The corrector-sampling comparison in Appendix B.6, Table 12, is already present in v1.

E3.justification: Both retain the 128/1024-token configurations, default 400k training updates, J1/J2 and generative-perplexity evaluations, and 5% character corruption for spelling correction. The detailed evaluation procedures and sampling-precision settings also match.

E4.justification: The roulette-parameter search in Table 5, bound comparisons, training-history analysis in Figure 8, precision/scorer comparisons in Tables 8–9, and generated examples in Appendix C are unchanged.

E5.justification: The Monte Carlo estimation procedures in Appendices B.4–B.5 and statistical reporting remain unchanged. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed disclosures, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted results, and generated examples match throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 1 retains CEDD* Absorb generative perplexity of 143.86, and Appendix Table 12 retains the corrector-flow value of 143.38.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–4, Propositions 5–7, and the definitions and derivations in Appendices A and D are unchanged. The paragraph break introduced within the Theorem 3 proof changes its presentation, not its reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: KL/cross-entropy results, the efficient perplexity bound, CEDD training, and roulette diffusion. Claims of up to 10% lower perplexity/generative perplexity and 15% faster training steps are unchanged.

C2.justification: Both retain the explanations of ratio-scale difficulties and rescaling, cautions about generative perplexity, and discussion of heuristic weighting and unexplored noise schedules. No interpretation, applicability boundary, or limitation is added or removed.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same architecture, H100 hardware, optimizer and hyperparameter disclosures, and implementation details. The code-access statement on page 1 is also unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the relationships to score-entropy training, earlier cross-entropy approaches, continuous-diffusion theory, and discrete flow matching.

P1.justification: The author line changes Gürbüz and Oğul to Gurbuz and Ogul, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. A paragraph is split in the Theorem 3 proof on page 17; the remaining wording and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: There are small equation-spacing, alignment, and text-reflow changes on pages 4, 17, and 24. Figures, tables, captions, and their placement remain unchanged; the embedded figure images match.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the same methods, proofs, experimental evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information, including the appendices. The author-name typography and localized paragraph/layout edits do not materially alter readability or scientific quality.
